description: Every fixture-matrix lane already runs fz2 --log-telemetry and reads the log back; fz-kdt.177.3 puts return_type.defined/.widened in that log. So the corpus widening sweep in drive_test.rs (which never read behavior/, drove the standalone semantic drive no door runs, and cost ~110 s per gate) is deleted rather than fixed. In its place the matrix folds each lane's log into the worst activation's (revisions, widened) and checks it: at or under a default ceiling of 5 with no widening unless the fixture header pins otherwise (a `return.ladder` header field beside diagnostic.code, checked in both directions). The six ladders (return_tuple_ladder, json_roundtrip, json_decode_cost, json_decode_control_bytes, json_decode_invalid_utf8, json_decode_surrogates) pin 17 widened. Zero extra compiles, three-door parity, pins live with the program; a fold may lower a pin, never raise one. Finding recorded on fz-kdt.177: standalone drive 277 activations / max 9 / 0 widened vs product pull 380 / 17 / 5 on json_roundtrip; the activation population drives the ladder.

comments.text: The three product-pull aborts pinned in CORPUS_PRODUCT_PULL_ABORTS are the ICE filed as fz-0rx; when it is fixed the pin empties and is deleted.

title: Return ladders are pinned per fixture on every door
